boxes.comments: Dark head number 37. The 3 has distinct upper and lower curves; the 7 has a rounded upper turn, long descending stroke, and separate rightward cross stroke. It belongs at the head and is recorded with mspage. Neighboring formula fragments are excluded.

Full formula I with low x-prime, literal equality, T with subscript infinity, parenthesized barred K, and a detached comma. I has heavy top and bottom bars; the x is low and the short prime sits immediately above/right of it. T has a long bar spanning both sides of its stem and a leftward terminal hook. Infinity has two joined loops. The overbar on K is detached. The head-number fragment at upper right is excluded.

Read cf plus haut. The c and long f are unseparated by punctuation; no detached stop follows cf. Plus has a p descender, looped l, low u and flattened final s. Haut has its tall initial h and terminal t; a separate dark stop follows the word. Abbreviation cf is not expanded.

Soit is legible, followed by a tall hooked f with a lower return and a low K with separate angled arms. At the middle of f, extra rounded/doubled strokes form a compact overlapping group. Live f is secure; the first alternative treats those strokes as part of its retracing. The second leaves one earlier compact group illegible under an uncertain overwrite state. No specific underlying letter is supplied. The illegible count denotes that one compact group, not a recovered character count. There is no secure final stop.

A tall K has a long left upright, rising upper diagonal, and distinct lower diagonal; it is followed by low un. The upper arm includes a small terminal retracing. No bar or hat is visible, and no punctuation is supplied.

Full local text U_K rat /K, retained literally. The U has an open hooked upper-left entry. Rat is abbreviated without a detached point: initial r downstroke/shoulder, compressed a-like return, and tall terminal t with a short right bar. The slash is detached before K, and the comma is separately visible after K. No expansion is supplied.

Full E_U_K expression, separate period, and Ceci posé. The last nested K has distinguishable angled arms. Ceci has a tall open C, looped e, low c, and dotted i. Posé has a p descender and a small final e with a detached, nearly horizontal acute to its upper right. No following comma or stop is secured.

Both ends of both arrows are visible in the full formula E_K to E_U_K to E_U. The first arrow has a clear right head and a raised psi label consisting of a cup and descending central stroke. The second short shaft ends in one small rightward head. The U forms have open entries, and the first two low base letters are K with angled arms. No extra index is visible on the final U.

One compact canceled label is covered by several diagonal hatch strokes. A left tall stem and low loop suggest b; two small raised strokes suggest paired primes; the large right closing curve supports a closing parenthesis. The whole tentative b-double-prime-parenthesis remains uncertain under cancellation. No following text is supplied.

The initial q has a closed head and long descender, followed by low u, apostrophe, dotted i, and tall l. A long low terminal return may include an s or may be the l exit stroke; qu-ils versus qu-il is therefore retained locally. Soient has a curved initial s, compressed o, dotted i, low en run, and terminal t rise/return. Clipped descenders of neighboring lines are excluded.

Literal impliques, with initial i mark, flattened m, p descender, tall l, dotted i, looped q with long descender, low u/e and a separate angular final s. No detached acute is securely visible above the terminal e; the spelling is retained without adding one. The vertical fragment entering from the preceding line is not treated as an accent.
Clair followed by a separate dark period. The c and looped l are large, a has a low closed body, i has a detached mark, and final r has a small shoulder. No final e is visible.

Tentative complete word aussitôt. The beginning is compressed into small open/curved and angular bodies; the dotted i and final tall t, rounded o with a separate curved circumflex-like mark, and last tall t/return are more recoverable. Because the early u/ss segmentation remains compressed, the whole word is marked unsure. Detached dark marks below the word have no secure letter or punctuation attachment and are not silently assigned to it.

Canceled d-un with a detached apostrophe. A low d loop and tall looped ascender survive the strike; after the apostrophe the low u cup and flattened n run remain visible. One long horizontal cancellation stroke spans the complete group. No terminal punctuation is supplied.

Full E_K = Gal barred-K vertical-bar K. The equality has two distinct strokes. Gal has a large G body, compressed a and tall l. No opening or closing parenthesis is secured around the arguments; the intervening vertical separator is preserved literally. The K overbar is detached. Lower-edge fragments belong to the insertion in B16 and are excluded.

Raised addition et E_S=(1). Both equality strokes and both parentheses around the single upright 1 are preserved. Its long curved leader runs from the right of the addition leftward and down to the gap after the baseline comma following d-inertie and before the live period/On. Both leader ends are visible. The baseline words, comma, period and On are context rather than part of this central inserted reading. The leader is not an underline or a closing parenthesis supplied to the baseline.

Compound revision: a long strike crosses de, genre, the g expression, and the terminal relation/comma. Genre is recoverable through the line; g has a deep descender. A short low group between g and the relation has an e/s-like horizontal body and a short t-like rise, tentatively est. The relation has an upper angled component and lower short bar before 1. A separate small raised fragment at the left begins with a loop and low rightward run, tentatively le with en as an alternative; its curved leader descends into the gap after the struck de and before genre. The large strike does not directly touch this raised fragment, so whether it was included in the canceled clause is explicitly unresolved. Above the right half, the live replacement reads U=X setminus T, X lisse, with open-entry U, two equals bars, a separate descending setminus stroke, and a T with its own broad top bar. The added line is uncrossed. A detached dark point below the end of this raised line and to the right of the cancellation is retained as doubtful punctuation; its attachment to the revised text remains unresolved. The serial order in the TSV records the local revision rather than claiming a settled chronology for the small raised fragment.

Raised continuation et propre. Initial et has a short open e and tall t. Propre retains both long p descenders, compact r/o bodies, terminal re return, and detached period. It sits between the neighboring main lines, continuing the raised replacement described in B17. No separate connector is visible inside this box; the clipped lower neighboring letters are not completed.

The full canceled word reads rationnelle: initial r/a forms, tall crossed t, detached i dot, o loop, two low n runs, small e, two separate looped l ascenders and terminal e. A horizontal strike crosses the entire word. Raised de has a low d loop/ascender and rightward e return; it is placed above the canceled word and replaces it before live X. The X to the right is uncrossed. No further text or punctuation is completed.

Conclusion has two initial low c/o forms, a flattened n, open c, tall l, low u/s, dotted i, and compressed on ending. The following complete word is tentatively est, but its first long downward stroke and highly flattened middle do not cleanly separate all letters; the tall terminal return is visible. The uncertainty is retained for that word alone. No punctuation is supplied.

Line-initial fragment is tentatively ment, followed by au. Its initial low bodies can be segmented as a flattened m; a short raised mark near the next compact return also leaves vient graphically possible. The long low middle run and tall terminal t are visible. The independently inspected B27 ends finale- on the preceding line, supporting the first fragment reading without joining or normalizing the source line break. The small a body and flat u of au are retained. No stop is visible.

Lemme is underlined once by a distinct stroke below the word extending slightly past its end. No detached point follows the heading. Soit follows with tall S and terminal crossed t. Neighboring lower-line fragments are excluded.

Literal abbreviation dim, with a low d loop and tall ascender, short i body, and compressed final m run. The last downturned stroke remains attached to the word; no separate abbreviation point is secured. No expansion is supplied.

Full local expression sur [overwritten base letter] trait. Both an S-like upper and lower curve and a T-like top bar/central upright are recoverable in the heavy overlapping ink. S is the current graphical preference, but the order of the overwrite is not secured; both canceled-T/live-S and canceled-S/live-T alternatives are retained. Trait is legible with first and final t stems, r shoulder, a loop and i dot. No punctuation is inserted around the base letter.

Relative 1 connexe, with no supplied comma. Relative has looped l, low a return, crossed t and dotted i, then v/e ending. The separate 1 has a vertical body and short baseline foot; it is an inline dimension numeral, not a page/formula label. Connexe has its low repeated n forms, crossed x and terminal e. The upper underline fragment belongs to Lemme and does not apply to this line.

Separate lower-left marginal foliation 74 in thin strokes. The 7 has a top bar, descending stroke, and crossbar; the 4 has an open upper form, horizontal arm and descending right stroke. It is retained as margin rather than head numbering.

Full visible line-final segment finale-: f has large upper and lower loops and a cross stroke, followed by short i, flattened n/a, tall l and terminal e return. The final horizontal hyphen is detached from the word at the line end and is preserved. The following-line fragment is separately recorded in B21; this box does not include it. Clipped neighboring strokes are not completed.

independence_attestation: I had not read this page in the first pass. I used only the generic blind-reader contract, the assigned original scan, the frozen box list, and the fresh crops made from that original. I opened no witnesses, first readings, page transcriptions, reviews, notes, notation lists, packets, other pages, or comparison files. Every prescribed crop was visually inspected directly. No OCR or text-recognition software was used.
method: The original was viewed once for layout. Each prescribed rectangle was cropped once from that original, autocontrasted, enlarged to 2800 pixels wide with LANCZOS, and mildly sharpened using UnsharpMask(radius=1.2, percent=110, threshold=3). All rotations are 0 degrees. Each saved crop was displayed and visually read once. No crop display was truncated; no crop was recreated or reopened. No mathematical expectations were used to supply missing ink.
return_policy: The TSV is fixed before reporting. No comparison was performed by this reader, and the returned files will remain unchanged.
